findings.issue_text: [BUG] UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only method introduced by this diff is the one-argument UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel), and UsernameForm extends AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator (not UsernamePasswordForm), so no no-arg overload exists in its hierarchy. The module fails to compile: 'cannot find symbol: method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()' in UsernameForm.java; the PR cannot build at all as diffed.

[ADVISORY] The reworked webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey test deletes the events.clear() that previously separated the initial passkey login from the first expectLogin assertion, leaving the initial login event (same user, same USER_VERIFICATION_CHECKED=true detail) pending in the events queue when the re-authentication event is asserted. events.expectLogin() polls the queue and can consume the stale initial-login event instead of the re-authentication event, making the assertion pass against the wrong event and masking a regression in the re-auth path; the author's rebuttal (the two events are identical so the test still passes) is true today but the assertion no longer verifies the re-authentication event specifically.

[BUG] UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but no zero-arg method of that name is defined in UsernameForm, AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, or anywhere in this diff — the only definition added is UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel), which UsernameForm does not extend. The module fails to compile as diffed (cannot resolve method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()), so the artifact as submitted is incomplete; either a definition hunk is silently missing from the diff or the call is wrong.

[ADVISORY] fillContextForm is now invoked unconditionally whenever passkeys are realm-enabled and a user is set, including re-authentication of users who hold no webauthn credential, but no branch handles the empty-authenticators case introduced by that call site (WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean.getAuthenticators().isEmpty() inside fillContextForm). A re-authenticating password-only user in a passkeys-enabled realm gets webauthn form data rendered for a credential type they do not own; correctness relies entirely on conditional-UI autofill gracefully no-oping in browsers, which is untested in this diff (the only no-passkey reauth test, reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey, disables passkeys at realm level, so the realm-enabled-but-user-has-no-passkey combination is never exercised).

[ADVISORY] The fix's core behavior — USERNAME_HIDDEN and REGISTRATION_DISABLED being re-applied on the error form after a failed re-authentication password attempt — is not asserted by any test in the diff; the new tests assert only the error message and continued webauthn form presence (webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey checks loginPage.getInputError() and the //form[@id='webauth'] element, never the hidden username field or absence of registration link). A regression that drops the setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError call from badPasswordHandler (i.e., re-introducing the bug this PR fixes) would pass the entire new test suite, leaving the acceptance criterion 'error form renders as re-authentication, not fresh login' unverified.

[BUG] UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only method defined in this diff (UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled, UsernamePasswordForm.java:160) takes a UserModel parameter, so the call site does not match any method introduced or shown here. Unless a no-arg overload already exists in unshown superclass code, this fails to compile (or resolves to an unintended overload), so the re-authentication passkey path in UsernameForm does not behave as the PR intends.

[BUG] The fillContextForm call in authenticate() was moved from a condition that ran when the user was NOT yet selected to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user), which requires user != null, exactly inverting the population of conditional-UI form data for the first-login (user==null) case. On the initial login page where no user is selected (the usernameless/discoverable-passkey discovery scenario), UsernamePasswordForm no longer sets the webauthn conditional-UI form attributes, so browsers relying on those attributes lose passkey autofill on first login; the old behavior for user==null is not preserved anywhere in this method.

[BUG] challenge(context, error, field) flipped from 'user == null' to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) (user != null), so the error-challenge path no longer sets webauthn data exactly in the case it previously did (user not yet identified, e.g. invalid username on first login). When a first-login attempt fails with an unknown/invalid username (user still null), the re-rendered challenge page loses the conditional-UI/passkey form data that the previous code set, regressing passkey availability on the error page for users who have not yet been identified.

[ADVISORY] The change widens USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH from protected to public solely so AuthenticatorUtils (a util class) can static-import it, creating a dependency from the util package back into the browser-authenticator package while WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator simultaneously depends on AuthenticatorUtils. A package-level cycle (browser -> util and util -> browser) and a public constant that is now part of the provider's API surface; the next refactor of the auth-note key or of AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator has one more cross-package place to update, and out-of-tree authenticators can now couple to this note.

[ADVISORY] setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError duplicates the boolean-from-authnote parsing pattern instead of reusing the existing AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth(context) helper, leaving two places that must agree on how the note is interpreted. If the note semantics ever change (e.g. non-'true' truthy values or a different note name), the error-path rendering in AuthenticatorUtils and the skip-clearing logic in AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator drift apart, producing a re-auth error page that shows the username field and registration link while the flow still treats the user as pre-set.

[ADVISORY] isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) conflates two independent conditions (passkeys feature/policy enabled AND user already identified) under a name that in the passkeys design means 'conditional UI' (user-less discovery), inviting misuse by future callers who expect the feature check alone. The next author calling this method to mean 'passkeys enabled for this realm' silently gets a false result for anonymous users, disabling passkey UI in a first-login context without any compile-time or test signal.

[ADVISORY] The new reauthentication tests duplicate the realm-policy setup, registration, first-login and event-assertion blocks across three tests in this class and across the parallel reauthentication tests in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest and PasskeysUsernameFormTest, instead of extracting a shared setup/verify helper. Any change to the passkeys realm policy setup (e.g. a new required policy field) must be edited in three or more near-identical blocks; the drift is already visible in that one copy was refactored into setPasswordlessPolicyForExternalKey() while the other two test classes still inline the same builder chain.

[ADVISORY] reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey asserts absence of the webauthn form via try { assertThat(...); fail(...) } catch (Exception nsee) {}, which swallows any exception (including assertion configuration errors) as a pass. If the locator or assertion itself breaks, the test silently reports success instead of verifying that passkeys UI is absent during re-authentication, weakening the exact negative case this test exists to guard.

[BUG] The webauthn conditional-UI setup in authenticate() was moved from a user==null condition to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) which requires user != null, inverting when passkeys data is filled for the no-user case. In a realm/flow where UsernamePasswordForm is reached with context.getUser() == null (e.g. the password form is the first browser execution, or a flow that skips UsernameForm), the conditional-UI form attributes are no longer populated on the initial challenge, so passkey autocompletion/conditional UI silently disappears for fresh logins — a regression of the behavior the old 'user is not already selected' branch explicitly provided.

[BUG] challenge(context, error, field) flipped its guard from context.getUser() == null to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) (user != null), so the two webauthn fill sites now cover disjoint user states with no site covering the complementary case. After a failed password attempt on a path where the context user was cleared (the state the old condition explicitly handled), webauthnAuth.fillContextForm is skipped and the error challenge page loses the passkey/conditional-UI controls that were present before this change; symmetrically, the user!=null case in authenticate() is now double-filled (authenticate and later error challenge both call fillContextForm), while the user==null case is covered by neither.

[ADVISORY] isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) is a third parallel predicate for 'passkeys active here' alongside UsernameForm's no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() and webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled(), each re-encoding the null-check and feature check slightly differently. The next passkeys condition added (or a change to what 'passkeys enabled' means, e.g. realm policy vs profile feature) must be replicated in each variant; a copy that forgets the user null-check or the webauthnAuth null-check reintroduces exactly the inverted-condition class of bug this diff fixed, and reviewers cannot tell from one site which predicate is canonical.

[ADVISORY] shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() hard-returns false unconditionally in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator, collapsing the isUserIdentified branch of the inherited fillContextForm into dead code for this subclass. The user!=null branch in WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm (WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean listing, empty-authenticators handling) is unreachable for the conditional-UI authenticator, so anyone reading fillContextForm believes authenticator listing can occur during passkey re-auth when it never can; a future change that needs the identified-user listing in the passwordless path silently no-ops via this override.

[ADVISORY] setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError keys re-auth form mode solely off the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth note, which is written only by the username/password form path, so the new call from WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse is a no-op whenever re-authentication entered via passkey without passing through the username/password authenticator. During passkey-only re-authentication that fails (the exact scenario this authenticator's error path serves), the note is unset and the error page renders as a fresh-login form (username visible, registration enabled) instead of re-authentication mode; the extracted helper centralizes the flag read but not the flag write, leaving the write site as the single implicit owner of the re-auth state.

[BUG] The webauthn form-data setup was moved out of the user==null branch and is now gated on isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) which requires user != null, so passkeys conditional UI is silently dropped on the initial username/password page where no user is identified — the exact case the removed comment ('setup webauthn data when the user is not already selected') existed to cover. On a realm with passkeys enabled, a fresh login through the username+password form no longer renders conditional-UI webauthn data before a user is selected, changing first-login behavior in a PR whose stated intent is only fixing re-authentication; the accompanying challenge() override has the same inversion (old code required context.getUser() == null, new code requires user != null).

[ADVISORY] The re-authentication fast-path (context.success() without showing any form) is now disabled for every user in a realm with passkeys enabled, not just users who actually have a passkey, since isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() gates on the realm feature, not on the user's credentials. Users with no passkey and no linked brokers in a passkeys-enabled realm silently lose the auto-re-authentication behavior (e.g. prompt=login previously completed without a form) and are now always shown a username form — a behavior change to the pre-existing happy path beyond the re-auth fix, with no test covering the user-without-passkey + realm-passkeys-enabled combination.

[ADVISORY] The test reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey claims to cover 'a user which does not have passkey' but actually disables passkeys realm-wide (setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)), so the untested gap is precisely the case the code change introduces: passkeys enabled at realm, user lacking a passkey. The scenario the new UsernameForm/UsernamePasswordForm gating most affects (feature on, user has no passkey, re-authentication) ships with no coverage, so a regression that breaks or degrades re-authentication for password-only users under a passkeys-enabled realm would pass CI.

[ADVISORY] The diff inverts an existing accepted test expectation: the old assertion (Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ... form[@id='webauth'])) encoded the previously accepted intent that passkeys are hidden on the username/password error page during first login, and the new assertions demand the opposite — an objective change to non-re-authentication login behavior smuggled in without a separate explicit acceptance. First-login behavior for realms with passkeys and organizations changes (webauthn form now shown after a failed password login even for non-discoverable keys); anyone relying on the documented/tested prior behavior of hiding passkeys on that page silently loses it, and the intent change is only visible as a flipped test assertion rather than a deliberate design decision.

[ADVISORY] setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError keys re-authentication form behavior solely on the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth note, which only AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator's flow sets, so any other flow reaching re-authentication error handling (e.g. a custom or IDP-brokered flow that sets the user without that note) renders the full registration/username form with the user's username pre-filled in the error challenge. A deployment using a non-default browser flow gets the re-authentication screen falling back to full-login rendering on error, exposing the previously-identified username in a challenge where the default flow hides it; behavioral divergence is silent because the guard is an untyped string auth note.

[ADVISORY] The internal auth-note key USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH is widened from protected to public and imported across packages, hard-wiring a session-state string constant into AuthenticatorUtils as a cross-module contract. Any code (including third-party authenticator extensions, now that the symbol is public API surface) can read or overwrite this auth note to toggle the hidden-username/registration-disabled rendering on the error form; the next rename or repurposing of the note becomes a compatibility break across all dependents.

[ADVISORY] The 'webauthn button absent' check wraps assertThat(element, nullValue()) plus fail() in a try/catch(Exception) that treats ANY exception as the expected outcome, so the guard asserts only that findElement threw something. fail("Not expected to have webauthn button") is unreachable dead code (assertThat throws AssertionError, not Exception, so it propagates past the catch rather than reaching fail), and any unrelated exception inside the try is silently swallowed as 'expected', weakening the negative assertion to 'an exception occurred'. The next reader modifying this block inherits a check that cannot fail for the stated reason.

[ADVISORY] The second 'webauthn button absent' check in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey repeats the same dead-fail/swallow-all-catch pattern as the first, asserting only that findElement threw some exception. Same as the first site: fail() is unreachable and the catch(Exception) classifies any exception (e.g., a driver/stale-element error) as the expected 'no webauthn button' outcome, so the re-authentication half of the negative case is verified only weakly.

[ADVISORY] webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey deletes the events.clear() that previously separated the initial login from subsequent event assertions, leaving the initial login event in the queue. The later events.expectLogin()...assertEvent() calls (for the passkey re-auth and the password re-auth) can be satisfied by the stale event from the initial login rather than the re-authentication event, so if the re-auth flow silently failed or fell back to a non-passkey path, the test still passes — the assertions do not prove the re-authentication event actually occurred.

[ADVISORY] The new AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context) call in createErrorResponse (the failed-passkey error path) has no test in the diff that triggers a passkey failure during re-authentication. If the re-auth note lookup or the USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED attributes are wired incorrectly on this path (e.g., the form re-shows the username field or the error page loses the webauthn form), no test fails; the diff's re-auth tests only exercise the success path and the password-failure path, not the passkey-failure error path added here. Test files checked: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java, PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java, PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.java — none drive an invalid-passkey error during prompt=login re-auth.

[BUG] The passkey/conditional-UI setup condition in UsernamePasswordForm is inverted for the not-yet-identified-user case: authenticate() previously called webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) whenever passkeys were enabled (no user check), and challenge(String,String) previously required context.getUser() == null; both now require context.getUser() != null via isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel), so the combined username+password login page rendered with user == null never gets webauthn data. In realms that use UsernamePasswordForm as the first (combined) login form with passkeys enabled, the initial login page and the error challenge after a failed login with an unknown username no longer render the webauthn conditional-UI form, so discoverable-key (resident-key) passkey authentication is silently unavailable on that page — a functional regression for first-login passkey users, not just a re-authentication change.

[ADVISORY] USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH is widened from protected to public solely so AuthenticatorUtils (a different package) can read the auth note, exposing an internal authenticator implementation detail as public API. Out-of-tree authenticators and future refactors can now depend on this constant and the auth-note contract it names; the stronger fix would be to move the note key (and the setup logic) into AuthenticatorUtils entirely, keeping the constant internal — the next change to this flag's semantics now has two public touchpoints to keep in sync.

[ADVISORY] badPasswordHandler now delegates to AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError, which duplicates the attribute-setting logic that the existing helper isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth encapsulates, leaving two parallel representations of the 'user was set before auth' check (the boolean helper and a raw auth-note read). The next change to how USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH is recorded (e.g., renaming the note or changing the flag's meaning) must be hunted down in both the helper-based and the raw-parseBoolean-based call sites; a missed one silently produces a form that shows the username field and registration link during re-authentication error pages — the exact bug this PR fixes, reintroduced on one path only.

[ADVISORY] isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) gates only on realm passkeys policy and user != null, not on whether the user actually possesses a webauthn/passkey credential, so webauthnAuth.fillContextForm and the conditional-UI flag are set up for password-only users in passkeys-enabled realms. Password-only users re-authenticating in a passkeys-enabled realm get a page with the conditional-UI flag and webauthn form scaffolding enabled even though no passkey credential exists for them; the browser autofill prompt silently never fires and the extra form markup is dead weight on every re-auth error page — debugging 'why doesn't my passkey prompt show' for these users starts from a misleadingly-enabled UI.

goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

adjudication.rationale: In `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest#webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey`, the initial passkey login (`webAuthnLoginPage.clickAuthenticate(); appPage.assertCurrent();`) is not followed by any `events.expectLogin()` at all, but the test *does* call `events.clear()` later (right before the first `events.expectLogin()` that asserts the re-auth passkey login). That `events.clear()` would remove any pending initial-login event from the queue, so the subsequent `events.expectLogin()` cannot consume the stale initial-login event as the finding claims.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `UsernameForm.authenticate()` now calling `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no args, but the unified diff only includes a small hunk from `UsernameForm.java` and does not show the rest of that file (or unchanged parts of `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java`). Since an unchanged zero-arg `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` could already exist elsewhere in `UsernameForm` or its superclass, the claim that the module “fails to compile as diffed” is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change when `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is called in `UsernamePasswordForm`: it is now invoked whenever `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true, i.e., when `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null` (new helper at bottom of `UsernamePasswordForm`), including re-authentication flows where `context.getUser()` is already set. The added tests cover re-auth with passkeys and a case where passkeys are disabled at realm level (`reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` sets `PasskeysEnabled` to false), but they do not exercise the realm-enabled / user-has-no-passkey combination the finding calls out. However, the claim that correctness depends on an unhandled `WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean.getAuthenticators().isEmpty()` branch is not verifiable from this diff: (1) `fillContextForm`’s full behavior isn’t shown, and (2) `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` explicitly overrides `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` to `false`, so the “show authenticators” empty-list path may not even execute for conditional UI. Net: there is a concrete, diff-grounded test/edge-case gap, but not a proven defect from the shown changes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff refactors the re-authentication error-form setup into `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` and calls it from `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler(...)` and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse(...)`, where it sets `LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN` and `REGISTRATION_DISABLED` based on the `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` auth note. The newly added/modified tests (e.g., `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey`, `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, and others) assert error text/info messages and presence/absence of the `//form[@id='webauth']` element, but do not assert that the username field is hidden or registration is disabled during re-authentication error rendering. Therefore, a regression removing the new setup call could plausibly pass these tests, making this a specific, diff-grounded missing-test concern rather than a direct defect shown in the code.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernameForm.authenticate`, the new condition calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments (`if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`). In the diff, the only newly added `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, and no no-arg overload is shown in `UsernameForm` or its visible code. If no such no-arg method already exists in `UsernameForm` or a superclass (not shown in the diff), this would be a compile-time error or could resolve to an unintended method, breaking the intended re-authentication/passkeys behavior.

When a first-login attempt fails with an unknown/invalid username (user still null), the re-rendered challenge page loses the conditional-UI/passkey form data that the previous code set, regressing passkey availability on the error page for users who have not yet been identified.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(context, error, field)` the condition was changed from `context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, and `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` explicitly requires `user != null`. This means the error-challenge path will no longer call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when the user is not identified (user is null), which is exactly the case the previous code handled (e.g., invalid/unknown username on first attempt). The diff shows no alternative call in that error path to preserve the passkeys/conditional UI setup when `context.getUser()` remains null, so passkey UI/data can regress on the re-rendered error page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The change widens USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH from protected to public solely so AuthenticatorUtils (a util class) can static-import it, creating a dependency from the util package back into the browser-authenticator package while WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator simultaneously depends on AuthenticatorUtils. A package-level cycle (browser -> util and util -> browser) and a public constant that is now part of the provider's API surface; the next refactor of the auth-note key or of AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator has one more cross-package place to update, and out-of-tree authenticators can now couple to this note.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` from `protected` to `public` (making it part of the public API surface), and `AuthenticatorUtils` now `static import`s it (`import static ...AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH;`). At the same time, browser authenticators call into `AuthenticatorUtils` (e.g., `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` both invoke `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(...)`). This is a concrete, diff-grounded cross-package coupling (util -> browser via the constant, and browser -> util via the new helper), which is an architecture/maintainability concern rather than an immediately verifiable runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError duplicates the boolean-from-authnote parsing pattern instead of reusing the existing AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth(context) helper, leaving two places that must agree on how the note is interpreted. If the note semantics ever change (e.g. non-'true' truthy values or a different note name), the error-path rendering in AuthenticatorUtils and the skip-clearing logic in AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator drift apart, producing a re-auth error page that shows the username field and registration link while the flow still treats the user as pre-set.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(...)`, which reads the auth note `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` and interprets it via `Boolean.parseBoolean(...)`. Previously, `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler` used the existing helper `isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth(context)` to drive the same UI behavior (hide username/disable registration). This introduces a second place that interprets the note instead of reusing the helper, creating a concrete maintainability/consistency risk (two implementations must stay aligned) even though no functional break is directly shown in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) conflates two independent conditions (passkeys feature/policy enabled AND user already identified) under a name that in the passkeys design means 'conditional UI' (user-less discovery), inviting misuse by future callers who expect the feature check alone. The next author calling this method to mean 'passkeys enabled for this realm' silently gets a false result for anonymous users, disabling passkey UI in a first-login context without any compile-time or test signal.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returning `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null;` and then uses it as the gate for setting up WebAuthn/passkeys form context in both `authenticate()` and `challenge()`. The method name suggests a feature/policy check (“conditional passkeys enabled”), but its implementation also depends on `user != null` (user-identified state). That is a maintainability/API clarity issue created by this change: a future caller could reasonably use it to mean “passkeys enabled in this realm,” and would silently get `false` for anonymous/first-step contexts due to the `user != null` clause. This is a concrete naming/semantic conflation visible in the diff, but not a directly verifiable functional defect in the current code paths as shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new reauthentication tests duplicate the realm-policy setup, registration, first-login and event-assertion blocks across three tests in this class and across the parallel reauthentication tests in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest and PasskeysUsernameFormTest, instead of extracting a shared setup/verify helper. Any change to the passkeys realm policy setup (e.g. a new required policy field) must be edited in three or more near-identical blocks; the drift is already visible in that one copy was refactored into setPasswordlessPolicyForExternalKey() while the other two test classes still inline the same builder chain.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows repeated, near-identical setup blocks in newly added reauthentication tests across multiple test classes: both PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest and PasskeysUsernameFormTest inline the same `getWebAuthnRealmUpdater().setWebAuthnPolicyRpEntityName(...).setWebAuthnPolicyRequireResidentKey(...).setWebAuthnPolicyUserVerificationRequirement(...).setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.TRUE).update()` chain plus similar “register user / logout / open login form / expectLogin” flows, while PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest partially refactors only one variant into `setPasswordlessPolicyForExternalKey()`. This creates a real maintenance/drift risk (already visible by uneven refactoring), but it’s not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey asserts absence of the webauthn form via try { assertThat(...); fail(...) } catch (Exception nsee) {}, which swallows any exception (including assertion configuration errors) as a pass. If the locator or assertion itself breaks, the test silently reports success instead of verifying that passkeys UI is absent during re-authentication, weakening the exact negative case this test exists to guard.

adjudication.rationale: In `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, the test checks absence of `//form[@id='webauth']` by calling `driver.findElement(...)` inside `try { ... fail(...) } catch (Exception nsee) { /* expected */ }`. This treats *any* exception from the lookup (e.g., `InvalidSelectorException`, WebDriver errors, unexpected runtime failures) as success, weakening the negative assertion. While `AssertionError` from `assertThat(..., nullValue())` / `fail()` would not be caught (since it’s not an `Exception`), the broad catch still risks masking real test breakage related to the locator/driver.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The webauthn conditional-UI setup in authenticate() was moved from a user==null condition to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) which requires user != null, inverting when passkeys data is filled for the no-user case. In a realm/flow where UsernamePasswordForm is reached with context.getUser() == null (e.g. the password form is the first browser execution, or a flow that skips UsernameForm), the conditional-UI form attributes are no longer populated on the initial challenge, so passkey autocompletion/conditional UI silently disappears for fresh logins — a regression of the behavior the old 'user is not already selected' branch explicitly provided.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm`, the conditional WebAuthn/passkeys setup was effectively inverted. Previously, the error challenge path explicitly populated WebAuthn form context when `context.getUser() == null` (`challenge(context, String error, String field)`), i.e., the “no user selected yet” case. After the change, both `authenticate()` and the error `challenge()` only call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true, and that helper requires `user != null`. This means flows that reach `UsernamePasswordForm` with no identified user (fresh login / password form first / flows skipping `UsernameForm`) will no longer get the WebAuthn conditional-UI attributes on the initial challenge or error challenge, plausibly removing conditional passkey UI/autocomplete compared to the prior behavior shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] challenge(context, error, field) flipped its guard from context.getUser() == null to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) (user != null), so the two webauthn fill sites now cover disjoint user states with no site covering the complementary case. After a failed password attempt on a path where the context user was cleared (the state the old condition explicitly handled), webauthnAuth.fillContextForm is skipped and the error challenge page loses the passkey/conditional-UI controls that were present before this change; symmetrically, the user!=null case in authenticate() is now double-filled (authenticate and later error challenge both call fillContextForm), while the user==null case is covered by neither.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm`, both places that populate passkeys/webauthn UI (`authenticate()` and `challenge(context, error, field)`) are now guarded by `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, which requires `user != null` (new method at bottom of the class). Previously, `challenge(context, error, field)` explicitly filled the webauthn context when `context.getUser() == null` and passkeys were enabled. With the new guard, when the user is not yet identified (typical for username/password form rendering) or when the user gets cleared on an error path, `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` will not be called anywhere in this authenticator, so the rendered challenge page can lose the conditional-passkey/webauthn controls compared to the old behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) is a third parallel predicate for 'passkeys active here' alongside UsernameForm's no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() and webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled(), each re-encoding the null-check and feature check slightly differently. The next passkeys condition added (or a change to what 'passkeys enabled' means, e.g. realm policy vs profile feature) must be replicated in each variant; a copy that forgets the user null-check or the webauthnAuth null-check reintroduces exactly the inverted-condition class of bug this diff fixed, and reviewers cannot tell from one site which predicate is canonical.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce/retain multiple slightly different “passkeys enabled here” predicates in different places: (1) `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` newly added checks `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`, (2) `UsernameForm` now gates behavior on `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (a different, no-arg predicate not shown here), and (3) other call sites still directly use `webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`/`webauthnAuth != null` patterns (e.g., prior logic was replaced in some spots but the underlying check still exists and is used inside the new helper). This is a maintainability/consistency risk (future changes to what “enabled” means may require updating multiple predicates), but it’s not a directly verifiable functional defect in the current diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() hard-returns false unconditionally in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator, collapsing the isUserIdentified branch of the inherited fillContextForm into dead code for this subclass. The user!=null branch in WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm (WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean listing, empty-authenticators handling) is unreachable for the conditional-UI authenticator, so anyone reading fillContextForm believes authenticator listing can occur during passkey re-auth when it never can; a future change that needs the identified-user listing in the passwordless path silently no-ops via this override.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm() to gate the user-identified authenticator listing logic on shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context). WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator overrides shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() to always return false, making the listing branch (WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean creation / empty-authenticators handling) unreachable for this subclass even when context.getUser() != null. This appears intentional (comment: "Do not show authenticators during login with conditional passkeys"), so it’s not a functional defect, but it does create a subclass-specific dead/disabled path that could mislead future maintainers or silently block future requirements that expect identified-user listing in the conditional-UI flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError keys re-auth form mode solely off the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth note, which is written only by the username/password form path, so the new call from WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse is a no-op whenever re-authentication entered via passkey without passing through the username/password authenticator. During passkey-only re-authentication that fails (the exact scenario this authenticator's error path serves), the note is unset and the error page renders as a fresh-login form (username visible, registration enabled) instead of re-authentication mode; the extracted helper centralizes the flag read but not the flag write, leaving the write site as the single implicit owner of the re-auth state.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError` bases its behavior solely on the auth note `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH`, and that `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse` now calls this helper. However, the finding’s key claim—that this auth note is “written only by the username/password form path” and therefore is unset for passkey-only re-authentication failures—cannot be verified from the provided diff because no write site for this auth note is shown here. Without evidence in the diff about where/when the note is set (or not set), the described broken re-auth UI rendering is not provable from this PR diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The webauthn form-data setup was moved out of the user==null branch and is now gated on isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) which requires user != null, so passkeys conditional UI is silently dropped on the initial username/password page where no user is identified — the exact case the removed comment ('setup webauthn data when the user is not already selected') existed to cover. On a realm with passkeys enabled, a fresh login through the username+password form no longer renders conditional-UI webauthn data before a user is selected, changing first-login behavior in a PR whose stated intent is only fixing re-authentication; the accompanying challenge() override has the same inversion (old code required context.getUser() == null, new code requires user != null).

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm`, the diff changes WebAuthn form setup from the prior condition `context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` (explicitly covering the “user not already selected” case) to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, and `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` explicitly requires `user != null`. The same inversion happens in `challenge(...)`. From the diff alone, this means a fresh login where `context.getUser()` is still null will no longer call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)`, dropping conditional-UI setup on the initial username/password page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The re-authentication fast-path (context.success() without showing any form) is now disabled for every user in a realm with passkeys enabled, not just users who actually have a passkey, since isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() gates on the realm feature, not on the user's credentials. Users with no passkey and no linked brokers in a passkeys-enabled realm silently lose the auto-re-authentication behavior (e.g. prompt=login previously completed without a form) and are now always shown a username form — a behavior change to the pre-existing happy path beyond the re-auth fix, with no test covering the user-without-passkey + realm-passkeys-enabled combination.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `UsernameForm.authenticate()` from `if (context.getUser() != null)` to `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`, which means the username-form “skip” fast-path for re-authentication is now additionally blocked whenever `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is true (diff does not show its implementation in `UsernameForm`). Separately, in `UsernamePasswordForm` the new `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` only checks realm/passkeys enablement + `user != null`, not whether the user actually has passkey credentials. Taken together, it’s a reasonable, diff-grounded concern that passkeys being enabled at realm level could disable the username fast-path for users without passkeys (behavior/UX regression scope), and the added tests do not cover the specific combination “realm passkeys enabled + user has no passkey”. However, this is not a clearly verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone (it may be intentional to surface passkey UI during re-auth).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The test reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey claims to cover 'a user which does not have passkey' but actually disables passkeys realm-wide (setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)), so the untested gap is precisely the case the code change introduces: passkeys enabled at realm, user lacking a passkey. The scenario the new UsernameForm/UsernamePasswordForm gating most affects (feature on, user has no passkey, re-authentication) ships with no coverage, so a regression that breaks or degrades re-authentication for password-only users under a passkeys-enabled realm would pass CI.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct that the diff adds/changes nontrivial conditional-passkeys behavior in re-authentication paths (e.g., `UsernameForm.authenticate` now skips auto-success when `context.getUser()!=null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`, and `UsernamePasswordForm` now fills WebAuthn conditional-UI context only when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` i.e., user != null). However, the added test `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` does not cover the important case “realm passkeys enabled but user has no passkey”; it explicitly sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)` (realm-wide off) and then asserts no `#webauth` form during re-auth. There is no test in the diff that exercises re-authentication for a password-only user while passkeys are enabled in the realm, so regressions in that scenario could slip through CI. (The finding’s statement that the test *claims* to cover a user without a passkey is somewhat off—the test comment says realm passkeys disabled—but the uncovered scenario remains real and diff-grounded.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff inverts an existing accepted test expectation: the old assertion (Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ... form[@id='webauth'])) encoded the previously accepted intent that passkeys are hidden on the username/password error page during first login, and the new assertions demand the opposite — an objective change to non-re-authentication login behavior smuggled in without a separate explicit acceptance. First-login behavior for realms with passkeys and organizations changes (webauthn form now shown after a failed password login even for non-discoverable keys); anyone relying on the documented/tested prior behavior of hiding passkeys on that page silently loses it, and the intent change is only visible as a flipped test assertion rather than a deliberate design decision.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does explicitly flip the UI/test expectation: in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey it changes from asserting the webauthn form is absent (Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException, find form[@id='webauth'])) to asserting it is present. This is backed by code changes in UsernamePasswordForm: webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) is now called whenever isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) (i.e., passkeys enabled and user != null), including after a bad password when the user is already identified, whereas previously webauthn form setup was gated differently. That is a concrete behavioral change (showing webauthn/passkeys elements on the username/password form for an already-identified user), but the diff itself doesn’t establish it as a correctness/security defect—rather it’s an intentional product/UX change that should be explicitly acknowledged/accepted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError keys re-authentication form behavior solely on the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth note, which only AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator's flow sets, so any other flow reaching re-authentication error handling (e.g. a custom or IDP-brokered flow that sets the user without that note) renders the full registration/username form with the user's username pre-filled in the error challenge. A deployment using a non-default browser flow gets the re-authentication screen falling back to full-login rendering on error, exposing the previously-identified username in a challenge where the default flow hides it; behavioral divergence is silent because the guard is an untyped string auth note.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` and uses it from both `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler(...)` and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse(...)`. That helper decides whether to hide username/disable registration solely by reading the string auth note `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` (via `context.getAuthenticationSession().getAuthNote(...)` and `Boolean.parseBoolean(...)`). From the diff alone we can verify the new behavior is gated only on that untyped auth note and there is no fallback based on `context.getUser()` or other signals. The finding’s broader claim about “only AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator’s flow sets” the note / “username pre-filled” in other flows isn’t directly verifiable from this diff, but the coupling to a specific auth note (now made `public` for external access) is a real, concrete integration/architecture concern introduced/centralized by this change rather than a definite defect in the default flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The internal auth-note key USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH is widened from protected to public and imported across packages, hard-wiring a session-state string constant into AuthenticatorUtils as a cross-module contract. Any code (including third-party authenticator extensions, now that the symbol is public API surface) can read or overwrite this auth note to toggle the hidden-username/registration-disabled rendering on the error form; the next rename or repurposing of the note becomes a compatibility break across all dependents.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly widens `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` from `protected` to `public` in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` and then makes `AuthenticatorUtils` depend on it via a static import (`import static ...USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH;`) to drive UI behavior (`USERNAME_HIDDEN`, `REGISTRATION_DISABLED`). This creates a cross-package contract on an auth-note string key and expands the public surface area such that other code can read/write the note, making future renames/semantic changes harder without breaking dependents. This is an architectural/compatibility concern rather than a directly verifiable runtime defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'webauthn button absent' check wraps assertThat(element, nullValue()) plus fail() in a try/catch(Exception) that treats ANY exception as the expected outcome, so the guard asserts only that findElement threw something. fail("Not expected to have webauthn button") is unreachable dead code (assertThat throws AssertionError, not Exception, so it propagates past the catch rather than reaching fail), and any unrelated exception inside the try is silently swallowed as 'expected', weakening the negative assertion to 'an exception occurred'. The next reader modifying this block inherits a check that cannot fail for the stated reason.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds negative checks like `try { MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail("Not expected..."); } catch (Exception ...) {}` in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey()`. As written, `findElement(...)` will either return a non-null WebElement (making `assertThat(..., nullValue())` fail with AssertionError, which is not caught) or throw (e.g., NoSuchElementException) which is caught and treated as expected. The `fail()` line is effectively unreachable because `findElement` won't return null, and the broad `catch (Exception)` can also mask unrelated exceptions by treating them as success. This is a real, diff-grounded test-quality issue, but it’s not a product/runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The second 'webauthn button absent' check in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey repeats the same dead-fail/swallow-all-catch pattern as the first, asserting only that findElement threw some exception. Same as the first site: fail() is unreachable and the catch(Exception) classifies any exception (e.g., a driver/stale-element error) as the expected 'no webauthn button' outcome, so the re-authentication half of the negative case is verified only weakly.

adjudication.rationale: In `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey()` the diff shows two identical checks using `try { MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail("Not expected to have webauthn button"); } catch (Exception nsee) { // expected }`. Since `driver.findElement(...)` throws when the element is absent, the `assertThat(..., nullValue())` (and thus the following `fail()`) is effectively unreachable in the expected case. Catching `Exception` also treats any Selenium/runtime failure (e.g., stale element, driver errors) as a success, weakening the negative assertion in both the initial login and the re-authentication half.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey deletes the events.clear() that previously separated the initial login from subsequent event assertions, leaving the initial login event in the queue. The later events.expectLogin()...assertEvent() calls (for the passkey re-auth and the password re-auth) can be satisfied by the stale event from the initial login rather than the re-authentication event, so if the re-auth flow silently failed or fell back to a non-passkey path, the test still passes — the assertions do not prove the re-authentication event actually occurred.

adjudication.rationale: In `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey`, although an earlier `events.clear()` was removed right after `logout()`, the test *does* call `events.clear()` immediately before each `events.expectLogin()...assertEvent()` that is meant to validate re-authentication: once right before `webAuthnLoginPage.clickAuthenticate()` (passkey re-auth), and again right before `loginPage.login(getPassword(USERNAME))` (password re-auth). Therefore, the later `expectLogin()` assertions cannot be satisfied by the initial login event, because that event is cleared from the queue before those assertions are made.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context) call in createErrorResponse (the failed-passkey error path) has no test in the diff that triggers a passkey failure during re-authentication. If the re-auth note lookup or the USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED attributes are wired incorrectly on this path (e.g., the form re-shows the username field or the error page loses the webauthn form), no test fails; the diff's re-auth tests only exercise the success path and the password-failure path, not the passkey-failure error path added here. Test files checked: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java, PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java, PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.java — none drive an invalid-passkey error during prompt=login re-auth.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new behavior in the failed-passkey error path: WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse() now calls AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context), which conditionally sets LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN and REGISTRATION_DISABLED based on the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth note. The added/modified tests exercise (a) re-authentication success via passkeys (prompt=login) and (b) password failure during re-authentication while passkeys UI remains available, but none of the tests shown drive a WebAuthn/passkey failure during prompt=login re-authentication that would execute createErrorResponse(). Therefore, if the note lookup or form attribute wiring is wrong on this specific error path, the current test changes would not catch it. This is a specific, diff-grounded test-gap issue rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The passkey/conditional-UI setup condition in UsernamePasswordForm is inverted for the not-yet-identified-user case: authenticate() previously called webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) whenever passkeys were enabled (no user check), and challenge(String,String) previously required context.getUser() == null; both now require context.getUser() != null via isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel), so the combined username+password login page rendered with user == null never gets webauthn data. In realms that use UsernamePasswordForm as the first (combined) login form with passkeys enabled, the initial login page and the error challenge after a failed login with an unknown username no longer render the webauthn conditional-UI form, so discoverable-key (resident-key) passkey authentication is silently unavailable on that page — a functional regression for first-login passkey users, not just a re-authentication change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes UsernamePasswordForm to only call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true, and that helper now explicitly requires `user != null` (`return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null;`). Previously, `authenticate()` filled the WebAuthn/passkeys context whenever passkeys were enabled (no user check), and `challenge(context, error, field)` did so specifically when `context.getUser() == null`. After this change, both paths skip filling WebAuthn data when `context.getUser()` is null, which is the common case for the initial render of the combined Username+Password form (user not yet identified) and for error challenges where the username is unknown. This matches the described regression: discoverable/conditional passkey UI can become unavailable on the initial combined login page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH is widened from protected to public solely so AuthenticatorUtils (a different package) can read the auth note, exposing an internal authenticator implementation detail as public API. Out-of-tree authenticators and future refactors can now depend on this constant and the auth-note contract it names; the stronger fix would be to move the note key (and the setup logic) into AuthenticatorUtils entirely, keeping the constant internal — the next change to this flag's semantics now has two public touchpoints to keep in sync.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly widens `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` from `protected` to `public` (line change shown), and `AuthenticatorUtils` (different package) then `static import`s it (`import static ...AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH;`) to read an auth note. This does expose an internal auth-note key as a public constant, making it easier for external/out-of-tree code to depend on that contract. It’s not a functional defect, but it is a concrete API/encapsulation/design concern created by the change and is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] badPasswordHandler now delegates to AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError, which duplicates the attribute-setting logic that the existing helper isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth encapsulates, leaving two parallel representations of the 'user was set before auth' check (the boolean helper and a raw auth-note read). The next change to how USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH is recorded (e.g., renaming the note or changing the flag's meaning) must be hunted down in both the helper-based and the raw-parseBoolean-based call sites; a missed one silently produces a form that shows the username field and registration link during re-authentication error pages — the exact bug this PR fixes, reintroduced on one path only.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the re-authentication form attribute setup was moved from an `if (isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth(context)) { ... }` block in `badPasswordHandler` into `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)`, which re-derives the condition by directly reading/parsing the auth note `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH`. The original boolean helper (`isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth`) still exists (the call site was removed but the helper was not shown as removed), so the condition is now represented in two places (a helper vs. a raw auth-note parse), creating a maintainability/consistency risk if the note semantics/key ever change. This is architectural/DRY debt rather than a verifiable functional bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) gates only on realm passkeys policy and user != null, not on whether the user actually possesses a webauthn/passkey credential, so webauthnAuth.fillContextForm and the conditional-UI flag are set up for password-only users in passkeys-enabled realms. Password-only users re-authenticating in a passkeys-enabled realm get a page with the conditional-UI flag and webauthn form scaffolding enabled even though no passkey credential exists for them; the browser autofill prompt silently never fires and the extra form markup is dead weight on every re-auth error page — debugging 'why doesn't my passkey prompt show' for these users starts from a misleadingly-enabled UI.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm`, `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` is defined as `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null` and is used to decide whether to call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` (both in `authenticate` and in `challenge(error, field)`). The diff shows no check that the identified `user` actually has any WebAuthn/passkey credential before setting up WebAuthn-related form context; so in a realm with passkeys enabled, any re-authentication where `context.getUser() != null` will run this setup even for password-only users. Whether that is a functional defect is not provable from the diff alone (it may be intentional and harmless), but it is a concrete, diff-grounded UX/behavior/scoping concern: potentially rendering WebAuthn/conditional-UI scaffolding when it cannot succeed for that user.
